Exercise 15.7.49 — Mass, Center of Mass, and Moment of Inertia

Problem. Let EEE be the solid in the first octant bounded by the cylinder x2+y2=1x^2 + y^2 = 1x2+y2=1 and the planes y=zy = zy=z, x=0x = 0x=0, and z=0z = 0z=0, with density function ρ(x,y,z)=1+x+y+z\rho(x,y,z) = 1 + x + y + zρ(x,y,z)=1+x+y+z. Use a computer algebra system to find the exact values of (a) the mass, (b) the center of mass, (c) the moment of inertia about the zzz-axis.

The center of mass is (xˉ,yˉ,zˉ)=(Myz/M, Mxz/M, Mxy/M)(\bar x, \bar y, \bar z) = (M_{yz}/M,\, M_{xz}/M,\, M_{xy}/M)(xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)=(Myz​/M,Mxz​/M,Mxy​/M).

Part 1 — The mass

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

The solid lies in the first octant under the cylinder x2+y2=1x^2 + y^2 = 1x2+y2=1, above the plane z=0z = 0z=0, and below the plane z=yz = yz=y. In polar coordinates in the xyxyxy-plane, x=rcos⁡θx = r\cos\thetax=rcosθ, y=rsin⁡θy = r\sin\thetay=rsinθ, the base is the quarter disk 0≤θ≤π/20 \le \theta \le \pi/20≤θ≤π/2, 0≤r≤10 \le r \le 10≤r≤1, and the height above each point is 0≤z≤y=rsin⁡θ0 \le z \le y = r\sin\theta0≤z≤y=rsinθ. Thus E={(r,θ,z):0≤θ≤π/2,  0≤r≤1,  0≤z≤rsin⁡θ}. E = \{(r,\theta,z): 0 \le \theta \le \pi/2,\; 0 \le r \le 1,\; 0 \le z \le r\sin\theta\}. E={(r,θ,z):0≤θ≤π/2,0≤r≤1,0≤z≤rsinθ}.

Step 1.2: Set up the mass integral.

With ρ=1+rcos⁡θ+rsin⁡θ+z\rho = 1 + r\cos\theta + r\sin\theta + zρ=1+rcosθ+rsinθ+z and the Jacobian factor rrr:

M=∫0π/2 ⁣∫01 ⁣∫0rsin⁡θ(1+rcos⁡θ+rsin⁡θ+z) r dz dr dθ. M = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^1\!\int_0^{r\sin\theta} (1 + r\cos\theta + r\sin\theta + z)\, r\, dz\, dr\, d\theta. M=∫0π/2​∫01​∫0rsinθ​(1+rcosθ+rsinθ+z)rdzdrdθ.

Step 1.3: Evaluate with SymPy.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates the iterated integral above with SymPy and independently re-evaluates the same mass in Cartesian order 0≤x≤10 \le x \le 10≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1−x20 \le y \le \sqrt{1 - x^2}0≤y≤1−x2​, 0≤z≤y0 \le z \le y0≤z≤y. Both orders return the same exact value:

M=3π32+1124≈0.7528576. M = \frac{3\pi}{32} + \frac{11}{24} \approx 0.7528576. M=323π​+2411​≈0.7528576.

Result (a). The mass is M=3π32+1124=9π+4496≈0.7528576. M = \frac{3\pi}{32} + \frac{11}{24} = \frac{9\pi + 44}{96} \approx 0.7528576. M=323π​+2411​=969π+44​≈0.7528576.

Part 2 — The center of mass

Step 2.1: Set up the first moments.

Each first moment multiplies the density by the corresponding coordinate and uses the same limits:

Myz=∭Ex ρ dV,Mxz=∭Ey ρ dV,Mxy=∭Ez ρ dV. M_{yz} = \iiint_E x\,\rho\, dV, \qquad M_{xz} = \iiint_E y\,\rho\, dV, \qquad M_{xy} = \iiint_E z\,\rho\, dV. Myz​=∭E​xρdV,Mxz​=∭E​yρdV,Mxy​=∭E​zρdV.

In polar coordinates the weights are x=rcos⁡θx = r\cos\thetax=rcosθ, y=rsin⁡θy = r\sin\thetay=rsinθ, z=zz = zz=z.

Step 2.2: Evaluate the moments and the coordinates.

The script solution/part2_step2.py evaluates all four integrals (mass and the three moments) with SymPy. The exact results are Myz=724,Mxz=π16+415,Mxy=π32+1390. M_{yz} = \frac{7}{24}, \qquad M_{xz} = \frac{\pi}{16} + \frac{4}{15}, \qquad M_{xy} = \frac{\pi}{32} + \frac{13}{90}. Myz​=247​,Mxz​=16π​+154​,Mxy​=32π​+9013​.

Dividing by M=(9π+44)/96M = (9\pi + 44)/96M=(9π+44)/96 and simplifying gives the center of mass:

xˉ=289π+44≈0.3874128,yˉ=2(15π+64)5(9π+44)≈0.6150116,zˉ=45π+20815(9π+44)≈0.3222644. \bar x = \frac{28}{9\pi + 44} \approx 0.3874128, \qquad \bar y = \frac{2(15\pi + 64)}{5(9\pi + 44)} \approx 0.6150116, \qquad \bar z = \frac{45\pi + 208}{15(9\pi + 44)} \approx 0.3222644. xˉ=9π+4428​≈0.3874128,yˉ​=5(9π+44)2(15π+64)​≈0.6150116,zˉ=15(9π+44)45π+208​≈0.3222644.

The script verifies the point lies inside the solid: 0≤xˉ≤10 \le \bar x \le 10≤xˉ≤1, 0≤yˉ≤10 \le \bar y \le 10≤yˉ​≤1, and 0≤zˉ≤yˉ0 \le \bar z \le \bar y0≤zˉ≤yˉ​ (indeed zˉ/yˉ≈0.524<1\bar z/\bar y \approx 0.524 < 1zˉ/yˉ​≈0.524<1).

Result (b). The center of mass is (xˉ,yˉ,zˉ)=(289π+44,  2(15π+64)5(9π+44),  45π+20815(9π+44))≈(0.387, 0.615, 0.322). (\bar x, \bar y, \bar z) = \left( \frac{28}{9\pi + 44},\; \frac{2(15\pi + 64)}{5(9\pi + 44)},\; \frac{45\pi + 208}{15(9\pi + 44)} \right) \approx (0.387,\, 0.615,\, 0.322). (xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)=(9π+4428​,5(9π+44)2(15π+64)​,15(9π+44)45π+208​)≈(0.387,0.615,0.322).

Part 3 — The moment of inertia about the z-axis

Step 3.1: Set up the integral.

The squared distance of (x,y,z)(x,y,z)(x,y,z) to the zzz-axis is x2+y2=r2x^2 + y^2 = r^2x2+y2=r2 in polar coordinates, so Iz=∫0π/2 ⁣∫01 ⁣∫0rsin⁡θr2(1+rcos⁡θ+rsin⁡θ+z) r dz dr dθ. I_z = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^1\!\int_0^{r\sin\theta} r^2 (1 + r\cos\theta + r\sin\theta + z)\, r\, dz\, dr\, d\theta. Iz​=∫0π/2​∫01​∫0rsinθ​r2(1+rcosθ+rsinθ+z)rdzdrdθ.

Step 3.2: Evaluate with SymPy.

The script solution/part3_step3.py evaluates this integral in polar order and checks it against the Cartesian order; both agree exactly:

Iz=π16+1760=15π+68480≈0.4796829. I_z = \frac{\pi}{16} + \frac{17}{60} = \frac{15\pi + 68}{480} \approx 0.4796829. Iz​=16π​+6017​=48015π+68​≈0.4796829.

Result (c). The moment of inertia about the zzz-axis is Iz=π16+1760≈0.4796829. I_z = \frac{\pi}{16} + \frac{17}{60} \approx 0.4796829. Iz​=16π​+6017​≈0.4796829.

Step 3.3: Verification by Python.

All quantities in Parts 1–3 were computed by the SymPy scripts solution/part1_step1.py, part2_step2.py, and part3_step3.py. Every integral was evaluated in two independent orders of integration (polar in the xyxyxy-plane with zzz innermost, and pure Cartesian), and SymPy confirms the two forms differ by exactly zero in each case. An independent high-precision numerical quadrature (mpmath, 30 digits) of the Cartesian form reproduces Myz=7/24M_{yz} = 7/24Myz​=7/24 and Mxz=π/16+4/15M_{xz} = \pi/16 + 4/15Mxz​=π/16+4/15 to all displayed digits.
